atlas · security

Agents get your access.
Never more.

Atlas runs as a pilot with a small number of teams. Everything on this page is true today.

Sign-in

People sign in through Clerk, with Slack. Workspaces are invitation-only, and there is no public sign-up.

One access check

The browser, the REST API and MCP share the same rules. Every request checks current membership and access, and search drops what you cannot open before it ranks results.

Agents sign in as a person

An agent gets its own OAuth grant after you approve it for one workspace. It never receives your browser session and reads only what you can read.

Narrow API keys

Keys for scheduled jobs cover chosen teamspaces, tables and metrics, and never exceed the access of the person who made them. If that person loses access, so does the key.

Agents propose, people approve

Agent edits arrive as change requests with a diff. Admins decide which roles may use each MCP tool, including approval.

Read-only warehouse

Warehouse queries are read-only and return a bounded number of rows. Free-form SQL needs access to every table.

Secrets and model calls

Warehouse, connector and model-provider credentials are stored encrypted and never returned by the API. Atlas sends content to a model only when a workflow you set up runs, with the provider and key you connect.

Audit and recovery

Changes, access grants and agent approvals are logged with who and when. Deleted pages go to a trash you can restore from, and any earlier version can be restored as a new one.

Where it runs

Ensemble Labs runs Atlas on Fly.io. The application and its PostgreSQL database are in Paris. Customers share one deployment, and each company is its own workspace.
